# Add Windows SSPI Backend

## Priority: Low 🟢
**Feature Enhancement for v0.3.0**

## Description

Implement Windows SSPI backend to provide native Kerberos support on Windows platforms, enabling cross-platform compatibility for kerbsec.

## Architecture

```
                  kerbsec API
                      |
            +---------+---------+
            |                   |
        Unix/Linux          Windows
            |                   |
        libgssapi             SSPI
            |                   |
    MIT/Heimdal Krb5      Windows LSA
```

## Requirements

### 1. SSPI Backend Module

```rust
// src/security/sspi.rs
#[cfg(windows)]
mod sspi {
    use windows_sys::Win32::Security::Authentication::Identity::*;
    use windows_sys::Win32::Security::Credentials::*;

    pub struct SspiContext {
        cred_handle: CredHandle,
        ctx_handle: CtxtHandle,
        established: bool,
    }

    impl SspiContext {
        pub fn new(config: KerberosConfig) -> Result<Self> {
            // Initialize SSPI
            let mut cred_handle = CredHandle::default();

            let status = unsafe {
                AcquireCredentialsHandleW(
                    ptr::null(),
                    NEGOSSP_NAME_W,
                    SECPKG_CRED_OUTBOUND,
                    ptr::null_mut(),
                    ptr::null_mut(),
                    None,
                    ptr::null_mut(),
                    &mut cred_handle,
                    ptr::null_mut(),
                )
            };

            check_sspi_status(status)?;

            Ok(Self {
                cred_handle,
                ctx_handle: CtxtHandle::default(),
                established: false,
            })
        }

        pub fn initial_token(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
            let mut output = SecBuffer {
                BufferType: SECBUFFER_TOKEN,
                cbBuffer: 0,
                pvBuffer: ptr::null_mut(),
            };

            let mut output_desc = SecBufferDesc {
                ulVersion: SECBUFFER_VERSION,
                cBuffers: 1,
                pBuffers: &mut output,
            };

            let status = unsafe {
                InitializeSecurityContextW(
                    &self.cred_handle,
                    ptr::null_mut(),
                    self.target_spn_wide(),
                    ISC_REQ_MUTUAL_AUTH | ISC_REQ_CONFIDENTIALITY,
                    0,
                    SECURITY_NATIVE_DREP,
                    ptr::null_mut(),
                    0,
                    &mut self.ctx_handle,
                    &mut output_desc,
                    &mut self.ctx_flags,
                    ptr::null_mut(),
                )
            };

            // Extract token
            let token = unsafe {
                std::slice::from_raw_parts(
                    output.pvBuffer as *const u8,
                    output.cbBuffer as usize,
                ).to_vec()
            };

            unsafe { FreeContextBuffer(output.pvBuffer) };

            Ok(token)
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. Platform Abstraction

```rust
// src/context.rs
pub struct Context {
    #[cfg(unix)]
    inner: GssContext,

    #[cfg(windows)]
    inner: SspiContext,

    config: KerberosConfig,
}

impl Context {
    pub fn new(config: KerberosConfig) -> Result<Self> {
        #[cfg(unix)]
        let inner = GssContext::new(config.clone())?;

        #[cfg(windows)]
        let inner = SspiContext::new(config.clone())?;

        Ok(Self { inner, config })
    }

    pub fn initial_token(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        self.inner.initial_token()
    }
}
```

### 3. Windows-Specific Features

#### Credential Management
```rust
pub enum WindowsCredential {
    /// Use current user's credentials
    CurrentUser,
    /// Use specific credentials
    Explicit {
        username: String,
        password: String,
        domain: Option<String>,
    },
    /// Use smart card
    SmartCard {
        reader: String,
        pin: String,
    },
}
```

#### SSPI Negotiation
```rust
pub struct SspiNegotiate {
    preferred_package: String, // "Kerberos", "Negotiate"
    delegation_enabled: bool,
    impersonation_level: ImpersonationLevel,
}
```

## Testing

### Windows CI
```yaml
# .github/workflows/windows.yml
name: Windows Tests

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Setup Rust
      uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

    - name: Test SSPI backend
      run: |
        cargo test --features windows-sspi
      env:
        TEST_DOMAIN: TESTLAB.LOCAL
        TEST_SPN: HOST/test.testlab.local
```

### Cross-Platform Tests
```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    #[test]
    fn test_context_creation() {
        let config = KerberosConfig::builder()
            .realm("TEST.REALM")
            .target_host("test.server")
            .build()
            .unwrap();

        let ctx = Context::new(config);

        #[cfg(unix)]
        assert!(ctx.is_ok() || ctx.is_err()); // May fail without krb5

        #[cfg(windows)]
        assert!(ctx.is_ok()); // Should always work on Windows
    }

    #[test]
    #[cfg(windows)]
    fn test_sspi_negotiate() {
        use windows_sys::Win32::Security::Authentication::Identity::*;

        let packages = enumerate_security_packages();
        assert!(packages.contains(&"Kerberos".to_string()));
        assert!(packages.contains(&"Negotiate".to_string()));
    }
}
```

## Documentation

### Platform Support Matrix
| Feature | Unix/Linux | Windows | macOS |
|---------|------------|---------|-------|
| MIT Kerberos | ✅ | ❌ | ⚠️ |
| Heimdal | ⚠️ | ❌ | ✅ |
| SSPI | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ |
| Keytab auth | ✅ | ⚠️ | ✅ |
| Smart card | ❌ | ✅ | ⚠️ |

### Usage Example
```rust
// Cross-platform code
let config = KerberosConfig::builder()
    .realm("CORP.EXAMPLE.COM")
    .target_host("server.corp.example.com")
    .build()?;

#[cfg(windows)]
{
    // Windows-specific: use current user
    config.set_windows_credential(WindowsCredential::CurrentUser);
}

#[cfg(unix)]
{
    // Unix-specific: use keytab
    config.set_keytab("/etc/krb5.keytab");
}

let mut ctx = Context::new(config)?;
let token = ctx.initial_token()?;
```
